title: runtime-agnostic onboarding criteria and soft-pin exemption flow for experimental weights
creator: Meera Shah
description: Problem: We accept community/open model weights that are flagged as 'experimental' or 'unverified'. Some variants are functionally compatible with runtime but intentionally left unpinned for rapid iteration. Current intake lacks clear acceptance criteria, compatibility signal expectations, and a documented soft-pin exemption flow, causing ad-hoc reviewer decisions and unexpected runtime failures or silent performance regressions.
goals: Define a runtime-agnostic acceptance matrix for experimental/unpinned open-model variants
Describe the soft-pin exemption flow that allows short-lived unpinned variants while protecting production customers
Specify required compatibility signals and minimal sanity tests for admission
Establish rollback and deprecation triggers tied to runtime telemetry and eval regressions
scope: This ticket defines the acceptance criteria, required artifacts, gating tests, and the operator flow for granting temporary soft-pin exemptions for open/experimental model variants in the catalog. It covers metadata fields, minimal evals, runtime compatibility signals, and an automated watchlist integration with Console. It does NOT change runtime fallback behavior or billing models (those are separate engineering tickets).
out_of_scope: Implementation of kernel-level runtime compatibility checks, changes to Dedicated autoscaling, pricing changes, or adding new telemetry agents to customer VPCs.
acceptance_criteria: A concise acceptance matrix (CSV) that maps model traits to minimum required artifacts (weights provenance, tokenizer, model card), with fields: compatibility_level, required_tests, max_allowed_latency_regression, and soft_pin_duration_days
Documented soft-pin exemption workflow that includes: request form template, reviewer checklist, automatic watchlist subscription, and approval TTL
A labeled set of runtime compatibility signals (cpu/gpu kernel mismatch, kv-cache shape mismatch, tokenization drift) and exact thresholds that trigger automated rollback/notifications
Integration plan for Console to surface soft-pinned variants with expiration and active watchlist entries
A step-by-step rollback runbook tied to runtime SLO breaches and quality-regression alerts
Stakeholder signoff from Runtime, QA, Security, and Developer Experience on the PRD
success_metrics: Reduce ad-hoc catalog reverts by 80% in the first quarter after rollout
Decrease post-ingest runtime incompatibility incidents for experimental variants by 70%
Time-to-decision for soft-pin requests under documented flow <= 48 hours for 90% of requests
Automated detection surface identifies >= 90% of incompatibility regressions within 1 hour of first failure
test_plan: Sanity evals: run existing smoke prompts (lang, tokenization, basic completions) and compare token-level alignment with a pinned baseline
Latency/throughput regression test on representative Dedicated and Hosted hardware profiles
Compatibility probes: verify kv-cache shapes, kv-cache replay round-trip, and attention-kernel selection matches expected model architecture
Canary run: route 0.5% of traffic via a canary path with automatic throttled fallbacks for 72 hours
Chaos scenario: simulate kernel mismatch (forced) and ensure alerting -> rollback sequence executes end-to-end
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Docs & Templates): publish acceptance matrix, reviewer checklist, and request form (Docs link below)
Phase 1 (Manual Ops): accept soft-pin exemptions manually for 2 weeks, collect reviewer feedback and telemetry mappings
Phase 2 (Console + Watchlist): add UI badge for soft-pinned variants and automatic watchlist subscription; enable expiration timers
Phase 3 (Automated Enforcement): wire runtime telemetry signals to automatic rollback triggers with human-in-the-loop notifications
Phase 4 (Retention): review metrics at 30/60/90 days and iterate matrix thresholds
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly permissive soft-pin durations increase risk of customer-facing regressions. Mitigation: default soft_pin_duration_days = 7 and force incremental renewals with explicit runtime evidence
Risk: Ambiguous compatibility signals lead to false positives. Mitigation: require two independent runtime signals or one signal + eval regression to trigger auto-rollback
Risk: Review bottleneck. Mitigation: create a rotating 'soft-pin on-call' roster and embed auto-accept heuristics for low-risk classes
required_artifacts: Model intake form (weights provenance URL, tokenizer spec, config file)
Minimal model card with intended use, known limitations, and test prompts
Smoke eval artifact (JSON) produced by Evals harness
decision_log: 2026-02-26: Proposed acceptance matrix reviewed with Runtime and QA; agreed to three-tier compatibility_level (low/medium/high)
2026-03-02: Security requested explicit provenance artifact for any unpinned variant > 3 days; added to matrix
2026-03-08: DX requested Console soft-pin badge; accepted and added to rollout plan
notes: Do not expose soft-pinned variants by default in public catalog search results; require 'include experimental' toggle
Consider a temporary 'experiment' namespace in the catalog to reduce accidental routing to production endpoints
Follow-up engineering tickets will formalize the telemetry to rollback mapping and the Console UI components
